chunks: And I found in the Ḥadīth of al-Ḥusayn ibn Mihrān al-Fārisī, from Muḥammad ibn Sayyār, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, who raised the Ḥadīth to al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him):
He said: Anyone who sells the clay of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), then he sells the flesh of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and buys it.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on selling the clay from the grave of Imam al-Husain (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) establishes the commercialization of the clay from the grave of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) as a distinct legal violation by equating its sale to selling his very flesh, thereby elevating the physical medium of the grave to a sacred extension of the Imam’s body. This hadith, found in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the Shia theological concept of *tawassul* and the sanctity of the Imams' physical remains, distinguishing the clay of al-Ḥusayn from other earths as a unique source of spiritual cure and reverence.
